ῥοδᾰνός , ή, όν, perh.
A.wavering, flickering, “παρὰ ῥοδανὸν δονακῆα”
Il. 18.576
:—this is the reading of most codd., but ancient critics differed as to the form; Zenod. gave διὰ ῥαδαλόν (which he derived from κραδαλόν); the reading of Aristoph. and Aristarch. is uncertain, perh. παρὰ ῥαδινόν, v. Sch. ad loc.; cf. also ῥαδινός ( Apollon. Lex. , who reads ῥαδινόν, absurdly interprets as λεπτόν, οἱονεὶ ῥαδονόν, παρὰ τὸ ῥᾳδίως δονεῖδθαι).
From A Greek-English Lexicon (Henry George Liddell, Robert Scott, Oxford, Clarendon Press, 1940)
